data.body:
Orchestrator close review — AC4 was WRONG and has been corrected; the implementation is right.

## The correction

AC4 originally read:

    A validated `daemon.json` change on a live daemon reloads Docker, never restarts.

That specifies behaviour that **cannot work**, and the implementation deliberately does the
opposite. From `infra/scripts/docker-storage-cap.sh`:

- `:92-93` — "dockerd's SIGHUP reload (`systemctl reload docker`) applies a fixed set of keys and
  `builder.gc` is NOT among them: the reload exits 0 and the GC policy [is not applied]".
- `:334-338` — the reload was REMOVED, and "its removal is the point rather than a tidy-up: a
  SIGHUP reload cannot apply builder.gc, so the only thing it ever produced here was a zero".
- `:143-145` — Docker is deliberately NOT auto-restarted (that would take Gerrit, the review-bot
  and the on-box MCP server down); the script instead warns INSTALLED-but-NOT-IN-EFFECT and
  points at the runbook for an operator-scheduled restart.

There is a test asserting exactly this: `test_a_reload_is_never_used_as_evidence_that_the_policy_took`.

So the AC asked for a reload that exits 0 while the policy is not in effect — another instance of
the *absence of execution reported as success* pattern this epic exists to remove. Rewriting the
AC to match the code is normally the wrong move; here the AC specified the defect and the code
refused it, so the AC is what changed. Recording the reasoning rather than silently editing.

## Every other AC verified against a named test, not asserted

- AC1 budget/split in one place — `test_print_env_states_the_whole_budget_and_its_split`,
  `test_the_split_follows_an_operator_override`, `test_a_buildkit_share_larger_than_the_budget_is_refused`
- AC2 engine-version schema — `test_modern_engines_get_max_used_space`,
  `test_older_engines_get_default_keep_storage`, `test_the_engine_version_is_probed_when_not_supplied`
- AC3 merge-before-start, backup/validate/restore — `test_compose_up_installs_the_cap_before_it_starts_docker`,
  `test_install_writes_the_policy_and_backs_up_what_was_there`, `test_a_rejected_config_changes_nothing`
- AC5 shared budget drives --keep-storage — `test_the_keep_storage_cap_comes_from_the_shared_budget`,
  `test_the_buildkit_cap_is_not_re_spelled_in_autodeploy`
- AC6 retention sweep — `test_the_retention_sweep_spares_the_serving_release_and_the_rollback`,
  `test_the_retention_sweep_never_forces_a_removal`, `test_the_retention_sweep_ignores_non_release_tags`
- AC7 publish-or-stay-silent — `test_a_failed_du_publishes_nothing_at_all`,
  `test_a_failed_docker_system_df_publishes_no_ledger_derived_metric`, `test_the_docker_metrics_carry_no_dimensions`
- AC8 alarms actioned + breaching — `test_every_alarm_declares_alarm_actions`,
  `test_host_alarms_treat_missing_data_as_breaching`, `test_breaching_host_alarms_are_wide_enough_not_to_flap`

My earlier note said ACs 3, 4 and 6 needed rewording. That was imprecise: 3 and 6 are satisfied
exactly as written. Only AC4 was wrong.

## Still operator-gated, and NOT claimed as done here

The `builder.gc` policy is INSTALLED but NOT IN EFFECT on the live host, by design — it applies
only at daemon start. Activating it needs an operator-scheduled `systemctl restart docker`, which
also sweeps roughly 1.0 GB of orphaned overlay2. That is deliberately outside this story: the code
obligation is to install correctly and report honestly, which it does.

## One thing worth flagging against this change

The 1205 outage investigation identified this story's own merge commit `bbe5d228bd2f` as a
possible AGGRAVATOR: it landed ~6.5 h before the outage onset and added two unconditional
`du -sx` walks over 17 GB of overlay2 per probe run, plausible dentry/inode pressure for the
page-cache eviction in that incident's H1. That is an unreproduced HYPOTHESIS, not a finding, and
it does not block this close — the du walks are how AC7's unaccounted-bytes metric is measured.
Recording it so it is not lost, and so the bounded-probe work in 1205 accounts for it.
